The Red Bull driver was heard branding Lawson and Lindblad “morons” as he struggled to lap the pair. Max Verstappen calls for FIA action over Racing Bulls ‘morons’ Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google for news you can trust Verstappen equalled his best result of the F1 2026 season in Hungary by finishing second as McLaren driver and reigning world champion Lando Norris took victory. The Budapest race saw Verstappen claim consecutive podium finishes for the first time in 2026 having finished third at the previous race in Belgium. An untelevised team radio snippet from Sunday’s race has revealed how Verstappen called for his Red Bull stablemates to be penalised. The footage, which cannot be reproduced here due to broadcast rights restrictions, shows Verstappen behind Lawson and Lindblad as the pair battle for position into Turn 2. Despite a blue panel flashing trackside to signify that a faster car is approaching, Lindblad and Lawson continue to fight as Verstappen closes in. Verstappen is heard saying: “Oh, they should get a penalty. This is f**king ridiculous, these morons! My God!” Lindblad and Lawson went on to finish eighth and 10th respectively. Analysis: Hungarian Grand Prix Hungarian GP conclusions: Norris afterglow, Piastri the nearly man, Newey insult Hungarian GP 2026 driver ratings: Norris delivers as Sainz hands Piastri nightmare blow Verstappen was not the only frontrunner to be frustrated by lapped traffic over the course of the Hungarian Grand Prix. Prior to his retirement with a gearbox problem, McLaren driver Oscar Piastri made contact with Carlos Sainz at Turn 2. Piastri was heard saying over team radio in the immediate aftermath: “Get out of the **** way, you idiot! Oh my God…” After the race, Sainz, who was handed a five-second time penalty for the incident, pointed to an issue “we were all having with the blue flags” with other drivers reporting that the blue flag system in the cockpit was not functioning normally. The FIA stewards confirmed in their report that Sainz “had been informed that Car 81 (Piastri) was approaching” prior to the collision. The stewards added that they decided against giving Sainz the standard 10-second penalty for what they described as “a mitigating factor.” The stewards explained: “At the point of the incident, the positioning of Car 55 relative to the circuit and the other cars meant that Car 81 was not visible to the driver of Car 55 prior to the attempted overtake. “Although the driver had been informed that Car 81 was approaching, the stewards accepted that the limited visibility reduced the degree of culpability. “Taking this mitigating circumstance into account, the stewards determined that a five-second time penalty, rather than the standard 10-second penalty, was appropriate.” Lewis Hamilton was also spotted making slight contact with Fernando Alonso as he made his way past after the Aston Martin slowed on the approach to Turn 2. https://telex.hu/english/2026/08/19/inve.text: Menü Kereső Investigation into money laundering allegations against Ukrainian cash couriers in Hungary closed by tax authority English Kovács Pál Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom The Criminal Directorate of the Hungarian National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) has closed the investigation into the Ukrainian cash transporters due to there being no evidence of a crime, attorney Dr. Lóránt Horváth, representing the Ukrainian bank Oschadbank, announced on Wednesday. According to the NAV, the cash and gold of unknown origin mentioned in the complaint, as well as the banknotes and gold seized during the inspection can be traced back to an interbank transaction between Raiffeisen Bank and Oschadbank; additionally, Raiffeisen Bank International AG has provided documentation verifying the origin of the banknotes and the precious metals which had been sold and were being transported, as well as the payment of the purchase price by Oschadbank. The criminal investigation has confirmed that the banknotes and the gold had not been obtained through criminal activity; and there was no doubt as to the lawful origin and source of the assets; therefore, in the absence of the legal elements of a crime, the act does not constitute a criminal offense, and no suspicion of any other criminal offense has arisen, stated Dr. Lóránt Horváth. The NAV had previously suspended the investigation in July. At that time, a decision to fully close the case had not yet been made, but they did announce that, based on the information available at that point, the cash transporters had not committed a crime. What is this case? On March 5, operatives of the Counterterrorism Center (Terrorelhárítási Központ-TEK) detained seven Ukrainian citizens near Budapest and seized gold and foreign currency worth more than 27 billion forints from the CIT vehicles they were escorting. According to the Prosecutor's Office, the unit was acting in response to a tip. It was later revealed that the source of the tip was one of the intelligence agencies, the Constitutional Protection Office, which was prompted by information received from another agency, the Information Office. The lawyer for the Ukrainian cash couriers later reported at a press conference that to their knowledge, and contrary to the official report, only members of the TEK were present during the raid, and that the NAV only initiated proceedings in the case later. According to the Ukrainians’ lawyer, the Ukrainian savings bank, Oschadbank, which was recipient, and the Austrian Raiffeisen Bank-which had sent the funds-, there was nothing unusual about the shipment, and the cash couriers were in possession of all the permits required for transporting the shipment from Austria to Ukraine. This did not prevent the Orbán government and its propaganda machine from claiming that there was a problem with the shipment, that money laundering may have been involved, and that the money might even be linked to the financing of the Tisza Party (which was in opposition at the time)—but to date, no evidence has been presented to support these accusations and insinuations. On March 10, a government decree was issued stating that “the legal title to the assets seized from the Ukrainian money-transporting vehicles could not be clarified on the spot.” Telex was the first to report that it was Viktor Orbán who had decided to intercept the Ukrainian “gold convoy,” and even the timing of the raid was decided at the highest levels of government. However, according to sources familiar with the details of the operation against the “gold convoy” who spoke to Telex, there was no professional justification for the raid. A prosecutor who was granted access to the secret service’s files concluded that “the Constitution Protection Office did not provide sufficient evidence to substantiate the claims of the shipment posing a risk to national security.” At the end of June, 444 reported that it had obtained a photo of an allegedly official document from the prosecutor’s office dated June 9, which lists the individuals whose involvement in the so-called “gold convoy” case needed to be clarified. The paper quotes the document, which names former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, Örs Farkas, the former state secretary overseeing national security services; János Hajdu, the former director general of the Counterterrorism Center; and Tamás Demeter, the former deputy chairman for criminal and law enforcement affairs at the National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) as the persons who “made substantive decisions and issued instructions". According to the newspaper’s sources, during his interrogation, Hajdu claimed that he had learned about the Ukrainian money couriers from State Secretary Örs Farkas. http://insidefutbol.com/2026/08/13/bojan.text: Scottish Football > Rangers Bojan Miovski On Bench – Rangers Team vs Jagiellonia Confirmed 13/08/2026 - 18:18 BST Jake Davies Ian MacNicol/Getty Images Fixture: Rangers vs Jagiellonia Competition: Europa League qualifiers Kick-off: 19:30 UK time Derek McInnes has picked his Rangers lineup vs Jagiellonia for this evening’s crucial Europa League qualifying clash at Ibrox – match preview here . The Gers went down to a 2-1 defeat in Poland in the first leg, leaving them with work to do this evening if they are to move a step closer to the Europa League league phase. Despite the loss, Rangers winger Findlay Curtis won praise for his fearless display in Poland . They will have to get the job done without striker Youssef Chermiti, who picked up an ACL injury in the weekend loss to Hibernian, putting him out for several months. Boss Derek McInnes is also coming under some early pressure, with six new signings in the team to face Hibernian, but a 2-1 loss suffered in the Scottish Premiership clash. The former Aberdeen manager will need no reminding just how vital it is that Rangers win tonight and progress past Jagiellonia. McInnes believes his side’s performance in the first leg was decent for the most part with Rangers shooting themselves in the foot. He has urged the Gers to deliver a big performance this evening in front of the Ibrox faithful. Jagiellonia also suffered defeat in league action at the weekend as they went down 2-0 to Widzew Lodz. McInnes picks Ivan Pandur in goal in the Rangers lineup vs Jagiellonia this evening, while in defence he goes with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya. Midfield will be an area McInnes knows Rangers will need to come out on top in and to get the job done he selects Dan Neil, Nicolas Raskin and Thelo Aasgaard, while Daisuke Yokota and Djeidi Gassama support Lawrence Shankland and Ryan Naderi. McInnes may want to shake up his Rangers lineup vs Jagiellonia at some point, throughout the 90 minutes or even extra time, and his options off the bench tonight include Bojan Miovski and Ross McCrorie. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6y8.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Garry Kasparov retired from competitive chess in 2005 to found political opposition movements in Russia By Alys Davies Published 1 October 2026 An exiled Russian opposition figure living in the US says he was warned by American and Lithuanian security services that his life was in danger. Former chess world champion Garry Kasparov said he was one of two dissidents told to take precautions, which he had done. His comments come after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment earlier this month charging five people who allegedly work for a network linked to the Kremlin with plotting attacks and murders in countries including the US, focusing on Russian dissidents and defectors. Kasparov wrote in his publication The Next Move that he had not been told explicitly that he and fellow Free Russia Forum co-founder Ivan Tyutrin were considered targets, but said both had been warned about their safety. Spanish newspaper El Mundo reported that it had obtained information that Kasparov, along with another Russian opposition figure, Ilya Ponomarev, had been warned about the plot over the summer by US authorities. Citing sources close to Kasparov, the paper said he had been placed under enhanced protection over the summer for the first time since he moved to the US. Kasparov wrote separately: "I will not stop and I will not hide, even if I thought it was possible to do so. "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as [Russian President Vladimir] Putin is in power in Russia - a circumstance shared by millions." Kasparov retired from competitive chess in 2005 to pursue a career in politics, founding movements that openly opposed Putin before fleeing Russia in 2013. He has not returned since. Russia classed him as a foreign agent following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and subsequently added him to a list of terrorists and extremists in 2024 - both categorisations he rejects. The other reported target, Ponomarev, was the only Russian MP who voted against the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014 and later went into exile in Ukraine. He declined to confirm or deny to the Moscow Times whether he had been tipped off about the alleged plot but said the allegations marked "a new level of escalation" by Russia. Image source, SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Image caption, Ilya Ponomarev was the only MP to vote against Russia's illegal annexation of Ukraine's Crimea in 2014 A network of individuals working for the Russian intelligence services has operated since at least 2024, the US Justice Department said. It said the so-called RIS Network had been conspiring and conducting attacks and murders on Russian dissidents and defectors around the world. Five alleged members of the network had been accused of operating "as part of a global assassination network that reached into the United States, attempting to recruit US citizens and foreigners to carry out killings at the behest of the Kremlin", Assistant Attorney General for national security John A Eisenberg said. The five people alleged to be responsible for organising the plots are Yuri Khrameev, Kirill Khrameev, Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, Yaidel Delgado Suarez and Angel Eduardo Castro. All five remain at large, the Justice Department said. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said when the indictment was unsealed that he would not comment on the charges until he had heard or seen "any credible evidence" or "tangible facts". Of the 110 announced closures, 70 contained, or contain, post offices. Photograph: Michael Kemp/Alamy Retail industry More than third of post offices in TG Jones stores to shut by early 2027 Closures within chain formerly under the WH Smith brand raise fears of high streets becoming ‘postal deserts’ Sarah Butler Sat 24 Oct 2026 02.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Towns and even city centres face being left as “postal deserts” after it emerged that more than a third of post offices within the troubled TG Jones chain are closing. So far this year 36 branches within the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith have closed and a further 34 are set to close by early 2027, according to Post Office records analysed by the Guardian. TG Jones was bought and renamed by Modella last year. Before the private equity group’s restructure won approval from creditors in July , the chain operated 180 post offices and it had been feared that as many as 60 could be closed under the shake-up. Up to 150 of the 450 stores acquired by Modella are expected to shut, about 65 of which have already closed and at least another 46 are to cease operating early next year. This total of 110 announced closures include the 70 containing post offices. The larger-than-expected wave of TG Jones branch closures follows an announcement in the summer that 52 post offices will close within Morrisons Daily convenience stores this year, some of which are close to the TG Jones sites. The move forms part of a wider plan by Morrisons to close 100 loss-making small stores. The raft of closures means that towns such as Stevenage in Hertfordshire, Bracknell in Berkshire and Orpington in Greater London, and some smaller cities including Hull and York are each losing two post offices in a matter of months. Telford’s last one is due to close in January. The majority of these lost sites replaced former crown post offices, the now almost entirely closed network of more than 100 directly operated large branches, which offered a full suite of services such as identity and passport checks, driving licence and banking operations. Some regions such as Essex, the West Midlands, Wales, Suffolk and Hertfordshire have been particularly hard hit. Six post offices in TG Jones stores in Essex are going, with Clacton-on-Sea and Brentwood shutting in January after the closure of ones in Basildon, Southend-on-Sea, Harlow and East Ham. Five are closing in the West Midlands and four in Wales. The Post Office is trying to find new operators in these locations but so far only Stirling has reopened after a TG Jones closure, and a permanent replacement for Ipswich is set to open in November. Temporary branches are to operate after TG Jones closures in Maidenhead and Uxbridge. Such losses can be devastating to the health of local economies. As the Post Office itself pointed out to a parliamentary inquiry into revitalising high streets, almost a third of small- and medium-sized businesses use their local branch at least once a week and more than half use the network at least once a month. Many small businesses report that losing this access would threaten their viability within months. After the closure of more than 6,800 bank branches across the UK, the Post Office “plays a critical role in protecting this essential service”, according to thetstate-owned company’s evidence to the inquiry. Post office operators already run 250 banking hubs, which combine services for several banking brands, across the UK. Mole Meade, a senior member at the CWU, the largest union for postal workers, said the closures would leave some areas as “postal deserts”. Meade added: “What we are seeing with the TG Jones closures is the continuation of a long-term strategy of cutting costs and chasing profit, with little regard for the communities that depend on post office services. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion “The CWU believes the Post Office should be focused on protecting and expanding access to services, not presiding over a continued reduction of the network.” The Post Office said: “We fully recognise the challenging trading conditions that TG Jones and many other high street retailers are facing at the moment. We proactively sought expressions of interest from our postmasters and partners to take on post offices within TG Jones stores that may close as a result of their restructuring plan or any decisions taken by landlords. “There is interest in taking on every location where it has been confirmed that a post office within a TG Jones store will close. In some locations there are over 40 applications from our postmasters who recognise the significant footfall operating a post office brings to their store … We’re committed to replacing every branch within a TG Jones store that closes and are working to progress applications as quickly as possible.” The state-owned Post Office – which is still reeling from the Horizon IT scandal – announced the closure of more than 100 branches in late 2024 . WH Smith travel stores in railway stations, hospitals and airports were not part of the Modella deal and remain owned by its original stock market-listed parent company. TG Jones was approached for comment.
